title: When Scope 3 Outruns the P&L
subtitle: IIM Bangalore’s FY 2024–25 BRSR study, SEBI’s FY 2026–27 assurance glide path, and the mid-cap CFO who still treats carbon as a footnote
description: An HBS-style teaching case set on 2 September 2026. After IIM Bangalore’s Supply Chain Management Centre published an analysis of 982 BRSR filings for FY 2024–25, and with SEBI’s BRSR Core assessment-or-assurance obligation reaching the top 1,000 listed entities in FY 2026–27, a composite mid-cap foundry CFO must recommend whether the board files and finishes, opens Scope 3 slowly, puts carbon and water into the capital plan, or waits for a peer. All national statistics and legal waypoints are taken from public sources.
